question: After the final-lock defect is fixed, should exec denylist policy remain persisted in both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json` with union/stricter-wins semantics?
rationale: Two operator-managed sources of privileged execution policy create a permanent ownership, upgrade, and recovery contract that code review cannot choose.

options.title: Choose one owner
options.body: Keep one canonical persisted denylist surface and migrate or derive the other path to avoid competing policy sources.

options.title: Accept dual surfaces
options.body: Approve both persisted surfaces with explicit precedence, recovery, hot-reload, and upgrade documentation.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer the feature if the dual-surface security and compatibility cost is not accepted.

recommendation.title: Choose one owner
recommendation.body: Keep one canonical persisted denylist surface and migrate or derive the other path to avoid competing policy sources.

likelyOwner.reason: The current authorization architecture and PR discussion both point to this owner.
